messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed Buchwald-Hartwig amination of 4-chloroanisole with 4-methylaniline; choose the ligand, base and isoxazole additive.

picks.reason: This tests the closest dibenzylamino-isoxazole analogue to the best-performing A11 under the leading ligand/base pair.
The dibenzylamino substituent may retain A11’s favorable effect, while its alternate ring position tests the positional dependence.
A8 gave a promising result with a different ligand/base pair, so testing it with the current leading pair can separate additive from catalyst effects.
This tests whether a simple phenyl substituent at the A11-like 5-position benefits the leading catalyst system.
This positional phenyl-isoxazole is a useful comparison to A1 under the leading catalyst system.
The fused benzisoxazole tests whether a rigid, fused heterocycle improves on the simpler isoxazoles.
This fused-ring isomer provides a direct test of how benzisoxazole connectivity affects the leading catalyst system.
This carboxylate-substituted isoxazole tests a distinct electronic profile under the best-performing ligand/base pair.
This small dimethylisoxazole tests whether simple alkyl substitution can reproduce the favorable effect seen with A11.
This less-substituted methylisoxazole tests whether A11’s additional pyrrolyl group is essential for its observed advantage.
This methyl-substituted ester isoxazole broadens the additive screen to a different substitution pattern under the leading pair.
This methyl/phenyl-substituted isoxazole tests a more hydrophobic analogue with the leading catalyst system.
This isoxazole ester tests whether an electron-withdrawing group can improve the reaction under the best-performing ligand/base pair.
The methoxy/ester-substituted isoxazole probes whether added donor substitution improves additive performance.
The difluorophenyl isoxazole tests a more electron-poor aryl substituent with the leading catalyst system.
This compact isoxazole ester tests a distinct ester placement under the leading catalyst/base conditions.
The furyl-substituted ester tests a heteroaryl additive while retaining the leading catalyst/base pair.
The thienyl analogue of A21 tests whether changing the heteroaryl substituent affects performance.
A11 has been the most consistently promising additive, and this fills the untested L1/B3 combination.
This tests the favored A11 additive with an untested base for L4 to check whether its weak prior results were condition-specific.
